summary: Excessive finalizer queueing causing 504s for ultra-large max_tokens on dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer SynthMail opened a ticket reporting repeated 504/stream cutoffs when calling the generation API with extremely large prefixes and a very large max_tokens budget. Calls are routed to a dedicated GPU pool reserved for the customer. Failures happen near finalization (88–95s after request start).

Impact:
- Multiple production customers using SynthMail's shared integration are experiencing request failures for long-document summarization flows.
- Error rate on the customer's integration spiked to ~18% on their dedicated pool during peak.
- Customer-facing SLA impact (enterprise contract).

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: d-pool-synthmail-us-east
- Serving runtime version: v2.11.4
- Model: redwood-alpha-7B (pinned)
- Request characteristics: input prefix ~85k tokens (concatenated docs), max_tokens requested: 120000, streaming enabled, stop tokens not set.

Steps to reproduce (from customer & internal repro):
1) POST /v1/generate to hosted endpoint with same API key and model pin to redwood-alpha-7B.
2) Body: prompt containing ~85k tokens of concatenated email threads + max_tokens:120000 and "stream":true.
3) Observe streaming for ~80s, finalization attempt, then a 504 or truncated stream at ~88–95s.

Observed behavior:
- Finalizer stage stalls, runtime emits repeated "finalizer timeout" logs and then the request is aborted with 504 returned by api-gateway.
- GPU memory and scheduling metrics show brief compaction spikes at time of finalization.
- Scheduler queue length for the dedicated pool jumps and some finalizer workers enter a retry/backoff loop.
- KV-cache evictions spike concurrently; however eviction count alone does not explain the finalizer delays.

Expected behavior:
- Long-running requests with large token budgets should either stream to completion within SLO or be throttled early with clear 429s instead of mid-finalizer 504s. Customers should get a graceful error explaining capacity/quota if request cannot be accommodated.

Logs / traces collected:
- Sample request id: req_20260313_synthmail_01 (attached traces in internal storage).
- Runtime log excerpt: "finalizer: waiting for GPU slot (timeout 90s)" repeated 6x before abort.
- Grafana links: latency: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serving/runtime-long-context?orgId=1&from=2026-03-13T10:00:00Z
- SRE trace: scheduler queue depth and worker restarts captured in run-log 2026-03-13/synthmail-finalizer.log.

Investigation notes (SRE/Eng):
- Reproduced with a local load test against the dedicated pool using the customer's payload shape.
- Root cause hypothesis: a confluence of factors causes finalizer-stage queueing to escalate: (A) the very large max_tokens increases finalization window and KV-merge work; (B) a scheduler bug in v2.11.4 allows finalizer tasks to be reprioritized behind canary model-reload compactions which occur on the same GPU nodes; (C) when compaction runs during finalization it temporarily reduces available encoder slots, causing retries and eventual gateway timeout.
- Memory snapshots near failure show a short-lived 8–12% GPU memory reclaim operation coinciding with compaction cron.
- There is an edge-case where two requests from the same customer trigger the routing layer to attempt a silent fallback to a variant model; that fallback path issues an additional KV load which amplifies pressure on the pool. This behavior is under investigation.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Lower max_tokens to <= 40k and split the job into streaming chunked calls; this reduced failures to <1% in customer's tests.
- Disable automatic fallback routing by pinning explicitly to the single model variant (workaround client-side).

Proposed remediation / next steps:
1) Immediate: schedule a controlled restart of one node in the dedicated pool to clear compaction backlog and apply a temporary cap for finalizer concurrent jobs for this pool (SRE action).
2) Short term (days): add defensive check to scheduler so background compaction tasks do not preempt finalizer workers.
3) Mid term (weeks): add pre-emptive capacity check that rejects very high max_tokens with a clear 429 and recommended chunking guidance; improve observability on finalizer queue latency.
4) Engineering follow-up: root-cause PR to fix scheduling priority logic and ensure fallback routing does not double-load KV for same-request fallback. PR referenced in related_github_prs.

Communications plan:
- Support notified customer of workaround and timeline; SRE will perform a maintenance window to restart a node tonight with customer approval.
- If the short-term changes mitigate the outage, we will plan a permanent fix on the next sprint.

Attachments:
- Attached internal reproduction script (repro_synthmail.sh) and runtime logs uploaded to internal artifact storage.
